question.problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)-{x}^{2},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)+2y⟩
$$

through the boundary of the square $0\le x\le 1,0\le y\le 1.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\,\text{d}A
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129319/assets/3786d0a5fb99d1a32d761e067f9c49b6b7da05a11fc555dd94a4ef42d753f129.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)-{x}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)+2y.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=-2x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the rectangular region $D$ as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2x+2)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2-2x)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[2x-{x}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(2-1)-0]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,dy \\  & =y\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
